text: The LORD said to Moses:
Command the Israelites and say to them: My offering, my food, my offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to me—be careful to present it to me at its appointed time.

versions.text: Command the Israelites and say to them: You are to be careful to present to me at its appointed time my offering, my food, my offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to me.
versions.explanation: The current word order piles three appositional phrases after the time expression, which is hard to follow when read aloud. Placing the object first (as in the Hebrew) restores the rhythm and clarity.

text: Say to them: This is the offering by fire that you are to present to the LORD: two flawless year-old lambs each day as a regular burnt offering.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight,
along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of pressed oil.
This is the regular burnt offering established at Mount Sinai, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
With it goes a drink offering of a quarter of a hin for each lamb; pour it out in the sanctuary as a drink offering of strong drink to the LORD.
Offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning—an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
On the Sabbath day, offer two flawless year-old lambs, together with two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and its drink offering.
This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
At the beginning of each month you are to present to the LORD a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven flawless year-old lambs,
with three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each bull, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for the ram,
and one tenth of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each lamb. This is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.

Their drink offerings shall be half a hin of wine for each bull, a third of a hin for the ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. This is the burnt offering for the beginning of each month, month by month throughout the year.

versions.text: Their drink offerings shall be half a hin of wine for each bull, a third of a hin for the ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. This is the burnt offering for every new moon throughout the year.
versions.explanation: Verse 11 renders the same expression as "at the beginning of each month," while this verse switches to "new moon," which may confuse hearers into thinking a different occasion is meant. Harmonizing the wording keeps the section consistent.

text: And one male goat is to be offered to the LORD as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its drink offering.
On the fourteenth day of the first month there is to be the LORD's Passover.
On the fifteenth day of that month there is to be a festival; for seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten.
On the first day hold a sacred assembly; you must do no laborious work.
Present to the LORD an offering by fire, a burnt offering: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs—see that they are flawless.
With each bull offer a grain offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, and with the ram two tenths;
with each of the seven lambs offer one tenth.
Include one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
Offer all this in addition to the morning burnt offering, which is part of the regular burnt offering.

versions.text: Offer all this in addition to the morning burnt offering, which belongs to the regular burnt offering.
versions.explanation: "Belongs to" is an odd, flat rendering of the Hebrew relative clause; "is part of" states the relationship clearly and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: In this way you are to offer each day for seven days the food of the offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD; it is to be offered in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the seventh day hold a sacred assembly; you must do no laborious work.
On the day of firstfruits, when you present to the LORD a grain offering from the new harvest during your Feast of Weeks, hold a sacred assembly; you must do no laborious work.
Present a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs,
with a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil—three tenths of an ephah for each bull, two tenths for the ram,
and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.
Include one male goat to make atonement for you.
Offer these in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. See that the animals are flawless, and present them with their drink offerings.
